topic: Efficiency, BHP, IHP, FHP, SHP, knocking and detonation
syllabus_extract: Efficiency, BHP, IHP, FHP, SHP, knocking and detonation. Ignition system, basic principles, description and operations
specific_objectives: 15.1.3.1 Trainees will be able to explain various engine power

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of engine power definitions and efficiency calculations using IB data; Instructor supervision required for calculation verification.
intro_questions: What is the difference between Indicated Horsepower and Brake Horsepower?
Define the term 'Friction Horsepower' in the context of piston engines.
Why is thermal efficiency a critical parameter for engine performance?

topics: Relationship between IHP, BHP, and FHP
development.content:
Definition of Indicated Horsepower (IHP)
Definition of Brake Horsepower (BHP)
Calculation of Friction Horsepower (FHP)
Relationship between IHP, BHP, and FHP
Concept of Mechanical Efficiency

Definition of Shaft Horsepower (SHP)
Calculation of Brake Thermal Efficiency
Identification of Knocking phenomena
Distinction between Knocking and Detonation
Causes and effects of Detonation

topics: Impact of detonation on engine components
Methods to prevent knocking and detonation
Role of octane rating in fuel selection
Effect of supercharging on detonation tendency
Summary of power definitions and efficiency metrics
development.content:

summary_questions: Explain how Friction Horsepower is derived from Indicated and Brake Horsepower.
Describe the primary difference between knocking and detonation in a piston engine.
List three operational factors that increase the tendency for detonation.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note comparing the operation of a simple float type carburetor with a modified carburetor, focusing on how fuel-air mixture control affects engine efficiency and detonation risk, as covered in the next lesson plan.
